risk_reasons: It creates a privileged admin identity — the authorization surface of the whole admin control plane
It writes public.users and admin_audit_log with the service_role key, outside any request-scoped gate
It runs against a shared Supabase project, so a mis-targeted invocation mutates the wrong environment
goal: One command mints a RepWorth admin identity end to end: it creates the Supabase Auth login, inserts the linked public.users row (role='admin', account_id NULL) and its admin_audit_log row in ONE Postgres transaction, refuses when either half already exists, prints a single-use recovery link and never a password, and refuses to run against a Supabase project the operator did not name.
non_goals: Revoking, resetting or enrolling existing admins — that is ticket #1182
A UI page or API route for minting; the service_role key makes this a script, per the ticket's Constraints
Any migration or schema change; admin_audit_log.actor_user_id stays NOT NULL and users keeps its role CHECK
MFA enrolment and the MFA_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED flip (#1182)
Any touch of impersonation, the dual-mode admin gate, src/proxy.ts, CORS or the Admin app
Repairing, re-linking or deleting an existing users row — the script refuses instead
A package.json script alias; the script is invoked with pnpm tsx like every sibling under scripts/

Running anything against the production Supabase project IN THIS RUN — the script now SUPPORTS production behind an explicit --env production plus a matching --confirm-ref, but this run never invokes it there
user_visible_behavior: An operator runs pnpm tsx scripts/mint-admin.ts --email <e> --name <n> --confirm-ref <project-ref> and the script prints TARGET (project ref, Supabase host, user@host:port database descriptor) before it writes anything
A successful mint prints the new users.id, the linked auth_id, and exactly one single-use recovery URL pointing at this app's /api/auth/callback with flow=admin and next=/admin/reset-password
A password is never generated, set or printed; the new admin sets one through the recovery link
--dry-run runs every refusal check and the target guard, prints the plan, and writes nothing to Postgres or Supabase Auth
Re-running for an email that already has a users row exits non-zero naming the existing row's id and role, and writes nothing

An email that already has a Supabase Auth login exits non-zero — in dry run on the read-only auth.users probe, and on a real run on the Auth API's own duplicate-email refusal; the half-succeeded hand process is reported and sent to the runbook, never silently adopted

A --confirm-ref that is not exactly the project ref parsed out of BOTH the Supabase URL host and the database connection target exits non-zero before any call; a partial or common substring is refused, and a production project ref is refused outright
--env staging maps the STAGING_-prefixed variables out of .env.staging.local so one command targets the staging project; with no --env the script uses the ambient environment
invariants: Invariant #8 — users.auth_id maps to the Supabase Auth identity, and SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY is read only inside this Node script, never by browser code
Invariants #12 and #15 — the script is the composition root: it builds its own postgres and Supabase clients from env and passes them into the domain helpers, which never import @/lib/db/server
admin_audit_log is written ONLY through writeAdminAuditLog (src/lib/audit/log.ts, migration 117) — never a raw INSERT
The users row and its admin_audit_log row commit together in ONE sql.begin transaction, or neither exists
admin_audit_log.actor_user_id stays NOT NULL and is satisfied without a migration: the minted admin is its own actor, resolved inside that same transaction
users.id has no default so the script supplies the UUID; users.auth_id is varchar; users.role obeys users_role_check ('owner','admin'); an admin's account_id is NULL
No new environment variable and no feature flag is introduced

Production is reachable ONLY behind an explicit --env production selector AND a --confirm-ref that equals the ref parsed from both halves of the target; ambient/local/staging modes can never reach a production project, and no mode defaults to production
edge_cases: A public.users row already exists for the email in any role — refuse, naming its id and role, before any Auth call

A Supabase Auth login already exists for the email with no matching public.users row — the half-succeeded hand process the ticket describes. Two independent refusals close it: a read-only auth.users probe that runs BEFORE the dry-run return (guarded by to_regclass, because the local and CI test databases provision no auth.users relation), and the duplicate-email error auth.admin.createUser returns on the real run

The auth.users probe is unavailable on the target — the run says so loudly, dry run reports that it could not verify the Auth half, and the real run still refuses on the Auth API's own duplicate-email error

The mint transaction rejects but the COMMIT actually landed (a lost acknowledgement) — the script reconciles by reading back the users row for the new auth_id and reports a successful mint only when that row carries THIS invocation's generated id; a row with a different id is a failure, never a mint

The mint transaction rejects with an AMBIGUOUS outcome (no SQLSTATE, or class 08 / 57) and the reconciliation read finds nothing — the transaction may still be in flight, so the Auth identity is PRESERVED and the run reports the uncertainty; the compensating delete runs only on a confirmed rollback (a MintRefusal this script raised, or a deterministic SQLSTATE in class 22, 23 or 42)
A reconciliation read that itself fails preserves the Auth identity and reports the uncertainty

Another users row already holds the freshly created auth_id — the refusal is reported and the Auth identity is PRESERVED, because deleting it would revoke a different admin's login; the reconciliation read runs before every compensating delete, with no special case for a refusal
A public.users row already exists for the resolved auth_id — refuse
The mint transaction fails after the Auth user was created — compensating auth.admin.deleteUser runs, and when that delete also fails the orphan auth id is printed for manual cleanup
generateLink fails after the transaction committed — the mint stands and the script tells the operator to re-issue a recovery link rather than re-mint
--confirm-ref is absent, or matches only the Supabase host and not the database target (a mismatched credential pair) — refuse before any write
STAGING_SUPABASE_URL is empty in .env.staging.local — the --env staging mapping falls back to STAGING_NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, as docs/runbooks/mfa-factor-reset.md records
Email is trimmed and lowercased before every comparison and before the INSERT, so casing cannot create a second identity for one human
The Supabase createUser call returns no user with no error — treated as a failure, not as a mint

rollback_plan: No migration, no flag, no schema change, and no runtime caller — the script is operator tooling. Roll back by reverting the squash commit on main. A mint already performed is undone by #1182's revoke path (revoke, never row deletion): the disposable staging smoke identity minted during verification is named in the PR body and in this run's report so the owner can revoke it; its rows are deliberately left in place.
observability: Every run prints TARGET (project ref, Supabase host, user@host:port database descriptor) before any write, and every refusal exits non-zero naming the reason — the script is interactive, so the terminal is the primary signal

The durable signal is the admin_audit_log row with event_type 'admin_minted': a users row with role='admin' and no matching audit row is the silent-failure shape, and it is exactly what the live-DB suite pins
